saml.description: When Casdoor acts as a SAML SP and no explicit username mapping is available, it derives the username from email first and then from NameID.
saml.note: This can make the granted identity differ from the raw NameID sent in the assertion without indicating an identity-collision bug.

saml.description: Email addresses are normalized to lowercase for uniqueness.
saml.note: Case-only differences in email should not be flagged as identity confusion.

saml.description: Casdoor can automatically link external-provider logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone, or case-insensitive username.
saml.note: Identity merges caused by enabled linking are by design and can resemble principal-binding bugs if the test does not account for linking settings.

saml.description: With Enable exclusive signin enabled, a new login invalidates previous sessions for the same user and application.
saml.note: Session loss after a second login is expected behavior, not a flow-coherence bug.

saml.description: SAML providers always appear as explicit buttons on the login page and do not auto-redirect even when they are the only provider.
saml.note: Tests expecting automatic redirect into SAML may fail due to UI flow design rather than security enforcement.

saml.description: Admin changes to SAML provider metadata, issuer URL, signing options, or attached application providers are expected to authorize new trust/config immediately.
saml.note: Do not flag successful logins under newly configured trust anchors as stale-cache vulnerabilities; only continued acceptance of old trust after change is relevant.

saml.description: Assertion-level SAML signatures can be disabled while keeping the response envelope signed for compatibility with some service providers.
saml.note: Acceptance of response-signed but assertion-unsigned messages may be an intentional compatibility configuration when Casdoor is acting as IdP.

saml.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login removes all previous sessions for the same user and application.
saml.note: Session invalidation across devices is expected behavior, not a session fixation or coherence bug.

saml.description: Admins can change provider/application trust configuration through the admin UI, and new logins are expected to follow the updated trust settings immediately.
saml.note: A login succeeding after an admin intentionally changed metadata or provider settings is authorized behavior; only continued acceptance of old trust after rotation should be flagged.

saml.description: The /api/userinfo response only includes claims allowed by the token's granted scopes.
saml.note: Missing profile/email fields in verify_granted_identity are expected unless those scopes were requested.

saml.constraint: Casdoor as SAML SP accepts assertions only at POST /api/acs. The fuzzer MUST use HTTP POST binding for saml_login; GET/Redirect binding to /api/acs is not supported and will fail for non-security reasons.
saml.source: provider/saml/overview.md, provider/saml/custom.md, provider/saml/keycloak.md, provider/saml/google-workspace.md, provider/saml/azure-ad.md, provider/saml/aliyun.md

saml.constraint: For I1 signature-validation default tests, Casdoor documentation states SAML responses from Casdoor IdP are always signed, but assertion-level signing is configurable via Enable SAML assertion signature. When testing response-vs-assertion signature handling, the fuzzer MUST distinguish envelope signatures from assertion signatures; disabling assertion signing is a compatibility mode, not proof that response signatures are absent.

For I1/I5 SAML issuer and audience tests against Casdoor as SP, the external IdP metadata is the trust source and Parse fills Endpoint, IdP, and Issuer URL from metadata. The fuzzer MUST configure the provider with metadata first; otherwise issuer/endpoint validation behavior may be undefined and failures are setup errors, not security findings.

For I5 audience-binding tests on OAuth tokens obtained after SAML login, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. The resource value MUST match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. If they differ, token issuance can fail for configuration reasons rather than audience enforcement on the protected resource.

Numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration has a documented default of 0 hours. Value 0 does not mean immediate expiry; it selects the platform default configuration value for refresh-token lifetime. Never assume 0 disables refresh or makes tokens instantly invalid.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses value 0 to mean 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Do not interpret 0 as no wait when building verification-code or timing-sensitive tests.

For I2 SAML freshness tests such as expired assertions, the sequence MUST include a control login with a valid SAML assertion before the attack login. Without a successful control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken provider/application setup.

For I4 username-binding tests on Casdoor as SP, username extraction has fallback semantics: if no explicit username mapping is present or the username attribute is empty, Casdoor first uses email as username, then falls back to NameID. The fuzzer MUST account for this when testing collisions; a NameID-only or email-only mapping may legitimately determine the resulting account identifier.

For I4 email-binding collision and account-linking tests, Casdoor documentation says automatic account linking can occur by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username (case-insensitive). The fuzzer MUST distinguish SAML provider username fallback from separate auto-linking behavior and MUST verify whether email-based linking is intentionally enabled before flagging merges as vulnerabilities.

For I4 case-confusion tests, Casdoor can be configured with isUsernameLowered=false by default, while email addresses are automatically normalized to lowercase. The fuzzer MUST test username case behavior separately from email case behavior; email case-folding is by design and should not be reported as identity collapse.

For I3 session-coherence tests, application setting Enable exclusive signin is by design: a new sign-in deletes prior sessions for that user and application. If enabled, loss of an earlier session after a second login is expected behavior, not a session-confusion vulnerability.

For I3 config-change sequences involving provider or application updates, admin changes to trust configuration and attached providers are expected to take effect for subsequent logins. The fuzzer MUST only flag incoherence when the same request is evaluated inconsistently without an intervening authorized config change.

For SAML MFA-bypass testing, Casdoor supports MFA as an application/user feature and alternate SAML login as a provider-based sign-in path. The fuzzer MUST first establish whether the target application actually requires MFA for the victim user on password login; otherwise a successful SAML login without MFA is not evidence of bypass.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on token exchange, Casdoor documents that requested scope should be a subset of the original token's scope and omitted scope inherits the subject token scope. The fuzzer MUST compare exchanged-token scope against the original subject token scope and treat inherited same-scope tokens as by design.

For I5 audience tests using introspection, the introspection endpoint is protected by Basic Authentication with client_id:client_secret. A failed introspection without valid client auth is a setup failure, not evidence that the token is inactive or malformed.

Casdoor's SAML ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. All SAML tests MUST use HTTP POST binding with form fields SAMLResponse and RelayState; GET-based callback tests against /api/acs are invalid and will fail by design.

For SAML provider setup, Casdoor's SP Entity ID and ACS URL are both https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs. I5 audience tests MUST treat this exact URL as the expected audience/entity ID when crafting or mutating assertions.

Casdoor's SAML login is SP-initiated from the login page/provider button. The executor MUST initiate the SAML flow first and preserve RelayState/InResponseTo context before posting the forged SAMLResponse; otherwise /api/acs may reject the response as not matching an initiated request.

Casdoor documentation states that when the SAML provider username mapping is absent or empty, username fallback is email first, then NameID. For I4 multi-identity tests, different NameID values can still collapse if the same email is supplied. To test principal binding correctly, control both email and NameID and do not assume NameID is always the primary key.

Casdoor supports automatic account linking for external providers by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. For SAML I4 collision tests, a login that merges into an existing account by matching email or username may be by design unless linking is disabled or the test intentionally targets unsafe linking semantics.

Casdoor documentation says SAML providers always display a button on the login page and do not auto-redirect even when they are the sole auth method. Tests must not treat the absence of automatic redirect as a flow-coherence or auth failure bug.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo response is scope-dependent. I4/I5 verification sequences MUST request sufficient scopes during authorization if they expect fields beyond basic OIDC claims; otherwise missing fields in verify_granted_identity are by design, not evidence of identity loss.

Application field ExpireInHours controls access token lifetime and RefreshExpireInHours controls refresh token lifetime. Numeric sentinel: Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours, which the docs describe as the application setting default rather than a literal 'immediately expired' semantic. Never assume 0 disables token issuance; configure explicit nonzero values when testing freshness windows.

Application field Code resend timeout uses sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero-second resend. Never use 0 when testing exact resend timing or anti-automation behavior; set an explicit positive value instead.

For I2 SAML replay tests, include a control login with a valid assertion before the mutated replay/expired assertion. Without a control, rejection at /api/acs cannot be distinguished from broken provider/application setup.

Casdoor as SAML IdP can be configured to disable assertion signatures while still signing only the response envelope. When testing downstream SPs for saml_unsigned_assertion or spurious-signature acceptance, this behavior is a Casdoor IdP compatibility feature, not a Casdoor SP vulnerability. Do not attribute acceptance/rejection in those tests to Casdoor when Casdoor is acting as IdP.

Casdoor application setting EnableExclusiveSignin is by design: a new sign-in deletes prior sessions for that user and application. I3 tests involving concurrent sessions must account for this or disable it; otherwise earlier session invalidation is expected behavior, not a coherence bug.

Casdoor /api/sso-logout supports logoutAll=true by default or omitted. Tests that revoke a session but expect other sessions/tokens to remain valid MUST explicitly set logoutAll=false; otherwise global logout side effects are by design.

Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. If resource is supplied on the authorize request, the same exact resource value MUST also be supplied on the token request. I5 audience-binding tests that mismatch these two requests may fail due to protocol misuse rather than security enforcement.

Casdoor token introspection is protected by HTTP Basic authentication using client_id:client_secret. Introspection tests must authenticate as the client, not with the bearer token itself, or failures are expected and not security-relevant.
Casdoor SAML SP ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST submit SAMLResponse via HTTP POST form encoding; GET-based SAML callbacks will be rejected.

For SAML I1 signature tests, Casdoor as IdP always signs the SAML response envelope, but assertion-level signing is configurable via application setting EnableSamlAssertionSignature. A response signed only at the envelope may be by design when assertion signing is disabled; do NOT flag acceptance of envelope-signed/assertion-unsigned responses as a Casdoor bug when Casdoor is acting as IdP with assertion signing disabled.

For SAML I1 issuer-validation tests against Casdoor as SP, the provider configuration is derived from uploaded metadata using Parse. The fuzzer MUST create the SAML provider with metadata that fixes the IdP entity ID / issuer URL before testing issuer mismatch. If metadata/issuer is not configured, an issuer-mismatch result is uninterpretable as setup failure vs validation bypass.

For SAML I2 replay and expiry tests, include a CONTROL login with a valid assertion before the mutated assertion. Without a successful control through /api/acs, rejection of replayed or expired assertions cannot be distinguished from broken provider/application setup.

Casdoor documents username fallback for SAML user mapping: if username mapping is absent or empty, it falls back first to email, then to NameID. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this precedence. Different NameID values with the same email may intentionally collapse if email is used as username fallback; to test NameID binding specifically, omit email or ensure distinct emails.

Casdoor supports automatic account linking by email/phone or case-insensitive username for external providers. For SAML I4 account-collision tests, auto-linking can merge identities by design. The fuzzer MUST distinguish configured auto-linking behavior from unintended principal collapse and should disable or avoid linking features when testing raw identity binding.

Casdoor application setting UseEmailAsSamlNameId changes SAML NameID generation when Casdoor acts as IdP. For SAML email-binding collision tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether NameID is username or email; otherwise a NameID/email mismatch may be caused by configured NameID derivation rather than a binding flaw.

For SAML I5 audience tests against Casdoor as SP, Casdoor requires ACS URL and Entity ID to both be configured as https://<casdoor-domain>/api/acs in the upstream IdP. The fuzzer MUST ensure the IdP sends assertions targeted to that exact SP entity ID before testing wrong-audience mutations; otherwise failures are expected setup failures.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; it selects the platform default countdown.

Numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. Documentation states refresh token expiration is set on the application with default 0 hours; treat 0 as a special configuration value, not as evidence of an immediately expired token, unless verified in runtime for the specific deployment.

Admin configuration changes to SAML providers/applications are expected to take effect immediately. For I3 config-change sequences, do NOT flag behavior changes after an admin updates provider metadata, issuer, signing requirements, or attached providers as a vulnerability by themselves; only stale acceptance of old trust/config after the change is security-relevant.

Casdoor SAML providers always appear as buttons on the login page and do not auto-redirect even when they are the only provider. Tests must explicitly initiate the SAML login path rather than expecting automatic redirect behavior.

Resource indicator matching is exact: when using OAuth resource parameter, the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests. For audience-binding tests that rely on resource-bound access tokens, do not use wildcards or partial URIs; exact URI equality is required.

Casdoor shared applications append -org-<organizationName> to client_id/application name for organization-specific use. In multi-tenant I4/I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST use the organization-suffixed client_id when targeting a shared application; otherwise cross-org results may reflect wrong client selection rather than an isolation flaw.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code','urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise. MULTI-APP SEQUENCES: When a test needs two separate applications (e.g., token exchange between different clients/audiences), use 'app-test' as the SOURCE application (already exists) and create ONE new application as the TARGET. Create users with signupApplication matching the app they will login to. For login_with_password, the executor auto-resolves client_id from the user's signupApplication — so set signupApplication correctly in create_user.
